list_entry.title: P’s argument is vulnerable to which

A.explanation:
Whenever we see Flaw answer choices start with takes for granted / presumes / fails to establish / fails to demonstrate they are presenting an idea that supposedly is something the author needed to assume but never established.

Did P need to assume that "the Phoenician alphabet alone could have provided the basis for the Greek alphabet"?

Not at all. First of all, that's a very extreme idea (the Phoenician alphabet alone could do it). More importantly, P is shooting down the hypothesis that the Greek alphabet was invented by someone who knew the Phoenician writing system.

So P doesn't need to assume anything that would help that hypothesis be true.

B.trap: Too Strong: first text ever Opposite
B.explanation:
This question is about P's argument. Was P assuming that "the first text ever written in Greek was a Homeric poem"?

No, the opposite. P is saying that this hypothesis is laughable.

C.explanation:
Out of Scope: requirements of oral/written

Neither person identifies anything that's required of a complex oral tradition or of a written language.

D.explanation:
Does P's argument attempt to demonstrate the truth of a hypothesis?

The opposite. P is arguing that a hypothesis is laughably untrue.

E.explanation:
Whenever a Flaw answer choice begins with fails to consider / overlooks the possibility the answer is presenting a supposed Objection.

Would it hurt P's argument to say, "maybe the person who invented the Greek alphabet was planning to teach it to others"?

Sure! P was saying, "Why would you bother writing down a poem you already know in a language that only you know?"

This answer choice is responding, "Because ... I was planning to then teach my new language to people. Then they could read the copy of Homer's epics that I wrote down in my new language".
